1: # 16 to 19 Bursary Fund
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: You could get a bursary to help with education-related costs if you’re aged 16 to 19 and:
6: 
7: - studying at a publicly funded school or college in England - not a university
8: - on a training course, including unpaid work experience
9: 
10: A publicly funded school is one that does not charge you for attending it.
11: 
12: There’s a different scheme in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
13: 
14: ### If you’re 19 and over
15: 
16: You could also get a bursary if you either:
17: 
18: - are continuing on a course you started aged 16 to 18 (known as being a ’19+ continuer’)
19: - have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP)
20: 
21: ### What a bursary is for
22: 
23: A bursary is money that you, or your education or training provider, can use to pay for things like:
24: 
25: - clothing, books and other equipment for your course
26: - transport and lunch on days you study or train
27: 
28: ## What you'll get
29: 
30: There are 2 types of 16 to 19 bursary:
31: 
32: - a bursary for students in vulnerable groups
33: - a discretionary bursary
34: 
35: ### Bursary for students in vulnerable groups
36: 
37: You could get a bursary worth up to £1,200, depending on your circumstances and benefits.
38: 
39: ### Discretionary bursary
40: 
41: You could get a discretionary bursary if you need financial help but do not qualify for a bursary for students in vulnerable groups. Your education or training provider decides how much you get and what it’s used for.
42: 
43: If you’re over 19, you’ll only be eligible for a discretionary bursary.
44: 
45: Your provider will decide how you get your bursary. You might get:
46: 
47: - an instalment paid by cash, cheque or bank transfer
48: - things like a travel pass, free meals or books
49: 
50: Some providers also offer one-off payments to cover study trips or travel for university interviews.
51: 
52: Your provider could stop payments if you break their rules, for example about attendance or how your bursary is used.
53: 
54: ## Eligibility
55: 
56: You must:
57: 
58: - be at least 16 and under 19 on 31 August 2021
59: - study at a publicly funded school or college, or be on an unpaid training course
60: - meet the residency requirements - your school or college can check this
61: 
62: ### Bursary for students in vulnerable groups
63: 
64: You may be able to get a bursary if at least one of the following applies:
65: 
66: - you’re in or you recently left local authority care
67: - you get Income Support or Universal Credit because you’re financially supporting yourself
68: - you get Disability Living Allowance (DLA) in your name and either Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit
69: - you get Personal Independence Payment (PIP) in your name and either ESA or Universal Credit
70: 
71: The amount you may get depends on the costs you have and what you need for your course. This might include money for books, equipment or travel costs to school or college.
72: 
73: ### Discretionary bursary
74: 
75: Your school or college will have their own criteria for discretionary bursaries. They’ll look at your individual circumstances - this usually includes your family income.
76: 
77: Ask student services about their criteria and any evidence you’ll need.
78: 
79: You can apply to a discretionary bursary if you’re over 19 and either:
80: 
81: - continuing on a course you started aged 16 to 18 (known as being a ‘19+ continuer’)
82: - have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP)
83: 
84: ## How to claim
85: 
86: Apply to your school, college or training provider. Ask student services or your tutor to explain what you need to do.
87: 
88: ### When to apply
89: 
90: Apply once you know where you’ll study or train, so you’ll get your bursary as soon as possible.
91: 
92: You might need to reapply for a bursary for each year of your course. Check with your provider.
93: 
94: ## Help
95: 
96: Your tutor or student services can help you decide if you’re eligible for a bursary and explain how to apply.
97: 
98: Contact the Education and Skills Funding Agency (ESFA) if your tutor or student services cannot answer your question.
99: 
100: ### You think a decision is unfair
101: 
102: Speak to student services if you’re unhappy with a decision. Follow their complaints process if you cannot resolve the problem.
103: 
104: ### Emergencies and hardship
105: 
106: You might be able to get more support if your circumstances change or you have an emergency. Your provider might also have a separate hardship fund. Speak to student services if you need extra help.
